title: ATOMIUM: Probing the inner wind of evolved O-rich stars with new, highly excited H<SUB>2</SUB>O and OH lines
question: (1) to identify and map the emission and absorption of H2O in several vibrational states, and of OH in Lambda-doubling transitions with similar excitation energies; and (2) to determine the physical conditions and kinematics in gas layers close to the extended atmosphere in a sample of asymptotic giant branch stars (AGBs) and red supergiants (RSGs).

data.arrays: main ALMA array, Atacama Compact Array (ACA)

what.value: Source coordinates, mass-loss rates, LSR velocities, pulsation periods, observation dates, and clean beams

evidence.quote: The source coordinates are obtained from the emission peak of 2D-Gaussian fits to the stellar continuum observed around 241.8 GHz with the ALMA extended configuration, see Table E.2 in Gottlieb et al. (2022).
The mass-loss rates in Table 1 are taken from Gottlieb et al. (2022); they are updated for GY Aql and IRC−10529 because of their revised distances.
Most of the adopted distances to the Mira and SR variables in Table 1 are extracted from the Gaia DR3 catalog (Gaia collaboration 2022)

what.value: Revised distances for GY Aql, U Her, and IRC-10529

evidence.quote: For U Her and IRC−10529 we have also adopted the best distance estimates from Andriantsaralaza et al. (2022)
( e ) Angular diameter from Table 1 of Montargès et al. (2023).

what.value: Spectroscopic rest frequencies for H2O and OH

evidence.loc: 3.2. Identification of highly excited water lines
evidence.quote: Using the JPL catalog (Pickett et al. 1998) 5 and the W2020 data base (Furtenbacher et al. 2020) and, limiting ourselves to energy levels up to ∼6500 cm −1 (9400 K), we have searched for all pure rotational or ro-vibrational dipolar electric transitions of water

external_data.citation: Pickett et al. (1998); Furtenbacher et al. (2020)

what.value: Earlier astronomical OH Lambda-doubling frequency measurements

evidence.quote: The Λ-doubling frequencies of OH derived from the ALMA observations in this work and in Khouri et al. (2019) are gathered in Table 4.

what.value: Laboratory rotational spectrum dataset for OH

evidence.quote: The data set from Drouin (2013) is available in the JPL catalog archive 23 .

recipe.goal: Extract spectra and measure line peak flux densities, velocity extents, and rest frequencies
recipe.method: Extract spectra from image cubes using circular apertures; measure peak flux density and velocity extent between 2.5 sigma line wings; average peak frequencies across stars corrected for systemic LSR velocity to derive rest frequencies.
key_parameters: Aperture diameters: 0.08 arcsec (high), 0.4 arcsec (mid), 4.0 arcsec (low); 2.5 sigma threshold for velocity extent
assumptions: Adopted stellar LSR systemic velocities from Table 1

recipe.goal: Improve spectroscopic OH Lambda-doubling rest frequencies
recipe.method: Combine ALMA OH transition frequencies from this work and Khouri et al. (2019) with the laboratory line list of Drouin (2013) and perform a Dunham fit using SPFIT.
key_parameters: 21 Lambda-doubling parameters for OH plus 5 isotopic breakdown parameters (2 poorly determined parameters out of 97 omitted)

recipe.goal: Measure angular sizes of H2O and OH emitting/absorbing regions and stack weak OH lines
recipe.method: Determine H2O sizes from geometric mean of max/min radii within 3 sigma contour and azimuthal averaging on moment 0 maps; fit 2D Gaussians to OH moment 0 maps within 3 sigma contour mask in CARTA; stack OH visibilities of four hyperfine transitions aligned in velocity to detect weak high-J OH lines.
key_parameters: 3 sigma contour threshold for size measurement and CARTA mask
assumptions: No beam deconvolution applied to irregular clean image sizes

recipe.goal: Fit compact H2O maser components and derive brightness temperatures
recipe.method: Fit 2D Gaussian components to channel maps using AIPS task SAD above 5 sigma threshold, group into maser features, and compute brightness temperatures from channel map peaks and deconvolved Gaussian component sizes.
key_parameters: 5 sigma extraction threshold; >= 3 neighboring components with ~2 km/s velocity coherence; peak S/N >= 10 for T_Gauss
assumptions: Maser emission has a Gaussian angular profile

recipe.goal: Derive excitation temperatures, column densities, line opacities, and OH/H2O abundance ratios from population diagrams
recipe.method: Construct population diagrams from velocity-integrated flux densities in 0.08 arcsec apertures for H2O and OH, perform linear least-squares fits to obtain T_ex (or T_rot) and N, calculate line-center opacities, and compute the N(OH)/N(H2O) ratio.
key_parameters: Circular aperture diameter = 0.08 arcsec; at least 6 lines for H2O; exclude masing 268.149 GHz line in AH Sco and IRC+10011
assumptions: Optically thin LTE emission uniformly filling a 0.08 arcsec circular aperture; spin degeneracy 3/4 (ortho) and 1/4 (para) for H2O; H2O and OH excited in similar regions; fractional abundance H2O/H2 = 3e-5 when estimating n(H2)

recipe.goal: Compare observations with H2O radiative transfer maser models and inner-wind chemical kinetic models
recipe.method: Examine slab-geometry radiative transfer maser models from Gray et al. (2016) across n(H2O), T_K, and T_dust to identify maser pumping regimes; run updated chemical kinetic models from Gobrecht et al. (2016, 2022) between 1 and 10 R_* at pulsation phases 0.2, 0.5, and 1.0 to compare with observed OH/H2O ratios.
key_parameters: Maser model: 411 ortho and 413 para H2O levels; Chemical model: radii 1-10 R_*, pulsation phases 0.2, 0.5, 1.0
assumptions: Slab geometry; ortho and para H2O treated separately without cross-species line overlap; fractional abundance H2O/H2 = 3e-5 in maser models
